title: No warrant to claim justification while persisting in unrepented sin
source_text: XXXIV. Nec etiam ulla controversia est, An aliquis legitime possit sibi persuadere se justificatum esse, & Deo gratum, qui tamen in se Dei amorem non sentiat, nec agnoscat fructus poenitentia dignos, sed perseveret in suis peccatis, absque vitae in melius mutandae proposito. Quicquid enim Protestantibus imputare soleant eorum adversarii, perpetuo illi docent & inculcant praesumptionem vanam & temerariam esse, si quis peccatis indulgens confidat se Deo placere, & per Dei misericordiam eximendum esse poenis, quas peccata ejus alioqui merentur: nec putant ullam veram fiduciam, & de gratia Dei certitudinem nasci, nisi ex conscientiae bonae testimonio, & dilectionis Dei experimento.
pass_a_gloss: Nor also is there any controversy whether someone can legitimately persuade himself that he is justified and pleasing to God who nevertheless does not feel in himself the love of God, nor acknowledges fruits worthy of repentance, but perseveres in his sins without a purpose of amending life for the better. For whatever their adversaries are accustomed to impute to Protestants, they perpetually teach and inculcate that it is a vain and rash presumption if anyone indulging sins trusts that he pleases God and is to be exempted by God’s mercy from the punishments which his sins otherwise merit: nor do they think any true trust and certainty concerning God’s grace arises except from the testimony of a good conscience and the experience of the love of God.
pass_b_english: Neither school licenses presuming justification while clinging to unrepented sin.
Protestants tie true assurance to a good conscience and love’s fruits, not carnal security.
